# Better Scholar 2.41.0 — guide for AI agents

Better Scholar is a Chrome extension for Google Scholar profile pages (scholar.google.*/citations). It colours the rows where the profile's owner is first, co-first, second or last author, adds venue rank chips (CCF 2026 and CORE/ICORE 2026 lists), award and talk chips (Oral, Spotlight, Highlight, best paper), and a panel with a role × rank table, filters, citation totals and copy / export buttons. Everything runs in the browser. What it asks of the network: Scholar's own pages (the "Show more" button when `autoLoad` is on, and a paper's page when the user presses the button that reads full author lists), and paper titles to Semantic Scholar when `semanticScholar` is on. Nothing else is sent.

Two things you can do:
1. **Set it up for the user** — decide the settings from what they ask for ("Settings" below) and give them one JSON object to paste.
2. **Read or drive it on an open profile page** — page events ("Page events" below); no setup needed.

## Set it up for the user

1. Read what the user wants. Use only the settings listed below; do not invent any.
2. Reply with **one JSON object** that holds only the settings to change, in the shape of the record under "Current settings" (nested objects, as in the examples; no dotted paths). Leave out what stays as it is.
3. The user pastes it into *Settings → Configuration & presets → Paste or edit a configuration (JSON)* and presses **Apply configuration** (or saves it as a `.json` file and uses *Import file*). The page then says what it applied and what it ignored. If something was ignored, ask the user to send you that message and correct the object.

Example — years chart off, BibTeX and summary buttons first, last-author rows only, bar-style rows:
```json
{"panel":{"years":{"show":false},"copy":{"order":["bibtex","summary"]}},"roles":{"first":false,"cofirst":false,"second":false,"last":true},"rows":{"style":"bar"}}
```

Rules:
- `semanticScholar` sends paper titles to a third party: turn it on only if the user asks for it. No preset touches it.
- The table of settings is in the order of the screen, top to bottom. `panel.show: false` hides the whole panel on the profile page; the settings of the table, of the awards and talks counts and of the copy buttons (`panel.table.*`, `panel.marks.*`, `panel.copy.*`) still decide what the toolbar popup shows, and every other `panel.*` setting has no effect then. A part's `show` switch hides the part, the switches inside it hide single things; the `order` lists only move things and never hide (a part left out of a list follows the others in the default order).
- The copy buttons, the table and the awards counts are also in the toolbar popup, under the same switches.
- What you see is what you search and copy: a rank list (CCF, CORE) or a kind of mark (award, oral, spotlight, highlight) that nothing draws — no chip (`rows.*`), no table tab (`panel.table.ccf`, `panel.table.core`), no count row (`panel.marks.*`) — is also left out of the search and of the exports.
- The counts follow the filters (`panel.filters.follow`, on by default): with a filter on, the panel's table, its awards and talks counts and its copy summary and copy table count the papers the narrowing filters leave (the years, the search, a venue, *Only highlighted*, the papers behind the h-index); the cell picked in the table and the awards row picked in the counts list papers but narrow no count. The toolbar popup counts every paper, and so do the `summary` and `export` calls unless they are given `filtered: true`.
- Colours are `"#rrggbb"` only; `""` restores the built-in colour of a role.
- A name (`labels.<message key>`) is a text of the screen in the user's own words — a title, a column, a button. It replaces the translated text in every language; `""` brings the built-in text back. Names are for the eye: the search operators (`role:first`), the exports and the page calls keep the standard words. A name is one line; control characters, invisible and zero-width characters, direction overrides, embeddings and isolates and the Unicode tag characters are removed from it (the left-to-right and right-to-left marks stay). The whole record has to fit Chrome's 8 KB for one synced item (a `<` counts six bytes): a configuration that would not is refused, with the reason.
- A language is a code from the list below. Changing `language` reloads the settings page.
- Not settings, so not in the JSON: the Semantic Scholar API key, the spellings of the user's name (kept per profile) and the cache of paper details; the user sets those on the settings page itself.

## Settings

| Path | Value | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `language` | "auto" or a language code | `"auto"` | Interface language of the extension. "auto" follows the browser; otherwise a language code. |
| `scholarLanguage` | "keep" or a language code | `"keep"` | Language Google Scholar pages are opened in. "keep" leaves the address alone; otherwise a language code (a page opened in another language is opened again in this one). |
| `roles.first` | true / false | `true` | Highlight the rows where you are the first author. |
| `roles.cofirst` | true / false | `true` | Highlight the rows where you are one of several co-first authors (equal-contribution marks such as * or †). |
| `roles.second` | true / false | `true` | Highlight the rows where you are the second author. |
| `roles.last` | true / false | `true` | Highlight the rows where you are the last author. |
| `rows.name` | true / false | `true` | Mark your own name in the author line of a highlighted row (bold, tinted). |
| `colors.first` | "#rrggbb" or "" | `""` | Row colour of the first-author role, "#rrggbb"; "" is the built-in blue. |
| `colors.cofirst` | "#rrggbb" or "" | `""` | Row colour of the co-first role, "#rrggbb"; "" is the built-in purple. |
| `colors.second` | "#rrggbb" or "" | `""` | Row colour of the second-author role, "#rrggbb"; "" is the built-in amber. |
| `colors.last` | "#rrggbb" or "" | `""` | Row colour of the last-author role, "#rrggbb"; "" is the built-in green. |
| `rows.style` | "full" / "bar" / "tint" / "none" | `"full"` | How a highlighted row looks: "full" is a tint and a bar at the left edge, "bar" the bar only, "tint" the tint only, "none" leaves the row as Scholar draws it. |
| `rows.ccf` | true / false | `true` | A CCF rank chip after the venue of a paper. |
| `rows.core` | true / false | `true` | A CORE rank chip after the venue of a paper. |
| `rows.prefer` | "ccf" / "core" / "both" | `"ccf"` | Where both lists rank a venue (CCF and CORE are often the same news twice): "ccf" draws the CCF chip alone and the CORE chip only where CCF has no rank for the venue, "core" the other way round, "both" draws both. The venue list of the panel and the notes of the BibTeX and Markdown copies follow; the table, the search and the other exports keep both lists. Only between lists that are drawn. |
| `rows.award` | true / false | `true` | An award chip (best paper and the like) on a paper. |
| `rows.oral` | true / false | `true` | An "Oral" chip (a talk level the authors wrote in the venue) on a paper. |
| `rows.spotlight` | true / false | `true` | A "Spotlight" chip on a paper. |
| `rows.highlight` | true / false | `true` | A "Highlight" chip on a paper. |
| `labels.mkBest` | text, at most 30 characters | `""` | The text of the chip of a best paper award (default: "Best paper"): your own words, in every language; "" brings the built-in text back. |
| `labels.mkBestStudent` | text, at most 30 characters | `""` | The text of the chip of a best student paper award (default: "Best student paper"): your own words, in every language; "" brings the built-in text back. |
| `labels.mkOutstanding` | text, at most 30 characters | `""` | The text of the chip of an outstanding paper award (default: "Outstanding paper"): your own words, in every language; "" brings the built-in text back. |
| `labels.mkDistinguished` | text, at most 30 characters | `""` | The text of the chip of a distinguished paper award (default: "Distinguished paper"): your own words, in every language; "" brings the built-in text back. |
| `labels.mkRunnerUp` | text, at most 30 characters | `""` | The text of the chip of an honorable mention (default: "Honorable mention"): your own words, in every language; "" brings the built-in text back. |
| `labels.mkTot` | text, at most 30 characters | `""` | The text of the chip of a test of time award (default: "Test of time"): your own words, in every language; "" brings the built-in text back. |
| `labels.mkFinalist` | text, at most 30 characters | `""` | The text of the chip of a best paper finalist (default: "Best paper finalist"): your own words, in every language; "" brings the built-in text back. |
| `chips.style` | "outline" / "soft" / "solid" / "text" | `"outline"` | How the chips are drawn: "outline" a border on white (rank chips) or a tint with a border (awards, talks), "soft" a tint without a border, "solid" a filled chip with readable text, "text" coloured words with no box. |
| `chips.shape` | "pill" / "square" | `"pill"` | The corners of the chips: "pill" fully rounded, "square" almost square. |
| `chips.label` | "full" / "tier" | `"full"` | The words of the rank chips: "full" the list and the tier (CCF A), "tier" the tier alone (A; the tooltip still names the list). |
| `colors.ccf` | "#rrggbb" or "" | `""` | Colour of the CCF chips, "#rrggbb"; "" is the built-in indigo (the weaker tiers fade towards grey). |
| `colors.core` | "#rrggbb" or "" | `""` | Colour of the CORE chips, "#rrggbb"; "" is the built-in indigo. |
| `colors.award` | "#rrggbb" or "" | `""` | Colour of the award chips, "#rrggbb"; "" is the built-in gold. |
| `colors.talk` | "#rrggbb" or "" | `""` | Colour of the talk chips (Oral, Spotlight, Highlight), "#rrggbb"; "" is the built-in slate. |
| `panel.show` | true / false | `true` | The panel in the right-hand column of the profile page: off hides all of it. The settings of the table, of the awards and talks counts and of the copy buttons still decide what the toolbar popup shows; every other panel.* setting has no effect then. |
| `panel.order` | list of ids | `["table","copy","marks","filters","metrics","years","venues","status","names"]` | The parts of the panel from top to bottom: a list of part ids (table, copy, marks, filters, metrics, years, venues, status, names). Ids left out follow in the default order; a part's own show switch hides it without changing its place. |
| `panel.header.name` | true / false | `true` | The panel's title at the top. |

| `panel.header.settings` | true / false | `true` | The button in the panel's title bar that opens the settings page. |
| `panel.header.fold` | true / false | `true` | The button that folds the panel to its title bar. Off: the panel is always open. |

| `labels.venuesTitle` | text, at most 30 characters | `""` | The text of the title of the venue list (default: "Where the highlighted papers appear"): your own words, in every language; "" brings the built-in text back. |
| `panel.status.show` | true / false | `true` | The status lines: how many papers are loaded, what could not be read, the button that reads full author lists. |
| `panel.status.loaded` | true / false | `true` | How many papers are loaded, and the Load all button. |
| `labels.loadAll` | text, at most 30 characters | `""` | The text of the Load all button (default: "Load all"): your own words, in every language; "" brings the built-in text back. |
| `panel.status.cutoff` | true / false | `true` | The papers whose author list Scholar cut off, and the button that reads the full lists. |
| `labels.resolveBtn` | text, at most 30 characters | `""` | The text of the Read full lists button (default: "Read full lists"): your own words, in every language; "" brings the built-in text back. |
| `panel.status.repeats` | true / false | `true` | The line about duplicate entries. |
| `panel.status.absent` | true / false | `true` | The line about papers whose author list does not name you. |
| `panel.status.unranked` | true / false | `true` | The list of papers at venues without a rank, with its Copy and Report buttons. |
| `panel.names.show` | true / false | `true` | Help with spellings of your name that Scholar prints differently. |
| `panel.names.hints` | true / false | `true` | The spellings of your name found in your papers, one click to add one. |
| `panel.names.add` | true / false | `true` | The box where you add a spelling by hand. |
| `labels.variantsTitle` | text, at most 30 characters | `""` | The text of the heading of the name help (default: "Name not matching? Add a spelling"): your own words, in every language; "" brings the built-in text back. |
| `hide.cited` | true / false | `false` | Hide Scholar's whole "Cited by" block in the right-hand column (table and chart). |
| `hide.citedTable` | true / false | `false` | Hide only the table of the "Cited by" block (All / Since …). No effect while hide.cited is on. |
| `hide.citedChart` | true / false | `false` | Hide only the year chart of the "Cited by" block. No effect while hide.cited is on. |
| `hide.coauthors` | true / false | `false` | Hide Scholar's "Co-authors" block. |
| `hide.access` | true / false | `false` | Hide Scholar's "Public access" block. |
| `mergeDuplicates` | true / false | `false` | Count a paper once when Scholar lists it twice (titles that differ only in capitals or punctuation). |
| `autoLoad` | true / false | `true` | Press Scholar's own "Show more" button until the whole paper list is loaded, as the profile opens. |
| `semanticScholar` | true / false | `false` | Ask Semantic Scholar's public API (paper titles only, no cookies) for a cut-off author list before opening the paper's Scholar page. Sends titles to a third party: leave off unless the user asks for it. |

Language codes: en (English), zh_CN (简体中文), zh_TW (繁體中文), ja (日本語), ko (한국어), es (Español), fr (Français), de (Deutsch), it (Italiano), pt_BR (Português (Brasil)), pt_PT (Português (Portugal)), ru (Русский), uk (Українська), pl (Polski), cs (Čeština), nl (Nederlands), sv (Svenska), da (Dansk), fi (Suomi), no (Norsk), tr (Türkçe), ar (العربية), he (עברית), hi (हिन्दी), id (Bahasa Indonesia), vi (Tiếng Việt), th (ไทย), el (Ελληνικά), hu (Magyar), ro (Română).

## Page events

On a profile page the extension marks the document with `data-rr-ready="true"` (on `<html>`) once it is running; a script on the page can then make calls. It reads what the page shows and sets the page's filters; it cannot read or change the settings.

Dispatch `better-scholar:request` on `document` with `detail: { id, method, params }`; the answer is a `better-scholar:response` event with `detail: { id, ok: true, result }` or `{ id, ok: false, error }`. `id` is a string or a number you choose; it comes back unchanged, so match answers to requests by it.
```js
const id = crypto.randomUUID();
const answer = new Promise((resolve) => {
  const on = (e) => { if (e.detail.id === id) { document.removeEventListener("better-scholar:response", on); resolve(e.detail); } };
  document.addEventListener("better-scholar:response", on);
});
document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("better-scholar:request", { detail: { id, method: "export", params: { format: "bibtex" } } }));
const { result } = await answer;   // result.text is the BibTeX
```

Calls:

### `ping`
Is the extension here, and what is it looking at?
Parameters: none.
Result: { version, owner, loaded, complete } — the extension's version, the profile's name, how many papers are loaded, and whether that is the whole list.

### `summary`
The numbers the panel shows: the role × rank tables, the awards and talks counts, the citation metrics. The tables and the counts are over every loaded paper unless `filtered` is true (the panel's own table follows the filters); `metrics.highlighted` follows the filters.
Parameters:
  - `filtered`: true: the tables and the awards and talks counts are of the papers the filters leave, as the panel counts them (when `panel.filters.follow` is on; `counted` then says how many papers that is, and the tables keep the rows of the whole profile); false (the default): every loaded paper.
Result: { owner, loaded, counted, shown, loadingAll, layoutBroken, edition, noRanks, mapped, summaries: { ccf, core, none }, marks, metrics: { highlighted, all } } — `counted` is the number of papers the tables are of; `mapped.<list>` the number of those papers whose rank in that list comes from the person's own venue mappings, not from the list;  `summaries.<list>` is { columns, rows: [{ role, A, B, …, total }], totals, hidden, absent, papers }; `marks` counts the papers by award or talk group (the groups the panel counts); `metrics.<which>` is { papers, citations, h, i10 }.

### `papers`
The papers, one record each: who you are in the author list, the venue's ranks, award and talk marks.
Parameters:
  - `filtered`: true (the default): only the papers the page shows now, after the filters; false: every loaded paper.
Result: { owner, total, papers: [{ id, title, authors, venue, pages?, year, citations, role, status, highlighted, type, me, rank: { ccf: { tier, name, mine? } | null, core: { rank, name, mine? } | null }, marks: [string], url }] } — `role` is first | cofirst | second | last | middle | null; `type` is conference | journal | null (the kind the rank lists give the venue); `me` is the profile owner's name as this paper's author line prints it (an empty text when it was not found); `mine: true` marks a rank from the person's own venue mappings, not from the list.

### `export`
The papers or the summary as text, in the format of a copy button.
Parameters:
  - `format` (required): summary: the summary as text · table: the summary table, tab-separated · papers: the papers, tab-separated · apa · ieee (a numbered IEEE reference list) · gbt (GB/T 7714-2015) · bibtex · markdown · json (the `papers` records) · csv (RFC 4180).
  - `source`: Which ranking summary and table use (default: the one the panel shows; none: by role only; a list that nothing draws is not used, the default is used instead). The other formats ignore it.
  - `html`: true: for table, papers, apa and ieee also return `html`, the same content for a word processor (a real table, real italics): what the copy buttons put on the clipboard next to the text.
  - `filtered`: true: summary and table count only the papers the filters leave, as the panel's own buttons do (when `panel.filters.follow` is on; the text then says what it counted); false (the default): every paper. The other formats always use the papers the page shows.
Result: { format, text, html? } — `html` only when asked for, and only for table, papers, apa, ieee and gbt (the references with the owner's name in bold when the page marks it).

### `filter`
Narrow the list the page shows (the filters of the panel). Only the filters named are changed; null clears a number.
Parameters:
  - `query`: The search box's text (syntax below); "" clears it.
  - `onlyHighlighted`: Only the papers where you hold a highlighted position.
  - `yearStart`: Papers from this year on.
  - `yearEnd`: Papers up to this year.
  - `minCitations`: Papers cited at least this often.
  - `impact`: The highlighted papers behind the h-index (at least h citations, h counted over the highlighted papers the other filters let through) or the i10-index (at least 10 citations).
Result: { shown, total, filters: { query, onlyHighlighted, yearStart, yearEnd, minCitations, impact }, errors, ignored } — `errors` names the terms of the query that could not be read (an operator with a value it does not take matches nothing); `ignored` names the filters asked for that were not applied because the settings leave them with no control on the page to undo them (the search box, the filter bar, the citation totals …).

### `clearFilters`
Remove every filter: the search, a table cell, an awards row, a venue, the year range.
Parameters: none.
Result: { shown, total, filters, errors } — as `filter` returns it (without `ignored`), after the filters are cleared.

## Search syntax

The search box and `filter { query }` take words and operators separated by spaces; a paper must match all of them. A word matches the title, authors, venue, the venue's name in the lists, the year, the role and the marks (case does not matter).

- `cites:>100` — citations compared with a number: > >= < <= = (a bare number means =).
- `year:>=2020` — the publication year compared the same way.
- `age:<5` — how old the paper is, in years, compared the same way: this year is 0, so age:<5 is this year and the four before it (the last five years; it stays true as the years go by).
- `ccf:a` — the venue's CCF rank: a, b or c.
- `core:a*` — the venue's CORE rank: a*, a, b or c.
- `role:first` — your position in the author list: first, cofirst, second, last, or middle (none of those four).
- `type:journal` — the kind of venue the rank lists say it is: conference or journal (a venue without a rank has no kind).
- `has:award` — has:award — a best-paper award or finalist mark; has:talk — an Oral, Spotlight or Highlight mark.

The values of `ccf`, `core`, `role`, `type`, `has` can be listed with commas: `role:first,last` is a paper where you are the first or the last author, `ccf:a,b` one at a CCF A or B venue. Separate words must all hold; the values of one word, any of them. The quick filters under the search box join the word of their operator in the same way.

## Rules for working on this repository

- Chrome first (Manifest V3). No build step and no runtime dependency: `src/` is loaded unpacked.
- `src/lib/` is pure: no DOM and no `chrome.*`. It is unit-tested in Node (`npm test`).
- Precision over recall in venue matching: a missing badge is fine, a wrong one is not.
- Privacy: no network request of the extension's own, except the user-triggered reads of Scholar pages and the opt-in Semantic Scholar title lookup. No analytics, no remote code.
- Every user-visible string is in all 30 `src/_locales/*/messages.json` files (tested). A setting is a row of `SETTINGS` in `src/lib/prefs.js`.
- Everything the extension adds to a Scholar page is prefixed `rr-`.
- Do not name competitors or other extensions in code, tests, commits or documentation.
- Commands: `npm test`, `npm run test:e2e` (Chromium against the stand-in Scholar server), `npm run data`, `npm run agents:doc` (regenerates this file).
